root_idea.summary: The root centers on a weapon or other means by which one fights, repels an enemy, or protects oneself.
root_idea.development: Alongside the weapon branch, the lexicon preserves a protective image in الإِسْلِيح: a plant associated with fattening camels and improving their condition, as though this gave them a weapon against slaughter. The root also developed several homonymous branches concerning excretion, plants, and military settings.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The Quranic form is the plural أَسْلِحَةٌ; the public dictionary headword is normalized to its supported singular citation form سِلَاحٌ.

senses.definition: A weapon or implement used for fighting, repelling an enemy, or defending oneself; weapons or arms.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic plural أَسْلِحَةٌ in 4:102 refers to the arms or defensive equipment carried by the fighting party. The term can include different implements of war rather than one particular weapon.

other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a person, bird, or other animal; the excrement may be described as thin.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To arm someone with a weapon or weapons.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The object may be armed with a particular implement such as a sword or bow.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cause camels to void thin excrement; to purge them.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of the effect of a herb or similar food on camels.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To rub a clarified-butter skin with سُلْح, an inspissated juice used to season it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a specialized preparation involving a skin or container for clarified butter.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cause someone to void thin excrement.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A causative excretion use, distinct in form from the Form II verb.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To arm oneself with, wear, or put on weapons.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Refers to taking weapons for one's own use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Excrement, dung, or ordure, especially thin excrement.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The expression يَا سَلْحَ الغُرَابِ uses the term figuratively as an insult meaning a foul or filthy person.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Rob or inspissated juice used to rub or season a skin for clarified butter.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized material use, not the weapon noun.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Rainwater left in pools by torrents.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This meaning is reported as a regional or lightly attested lexical usage.
A collective bird-term, with a corresponding singulative form reported in the lexical discussion.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A loosening or flux of thin excrement; diarrhea.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A bodily-condition sense related to the excrement branch.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The horns of a bull, figuratively regarded as its weapons.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative conventional expression applied to the bull's horns.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An appellation for Arcturus, the star also called السَّمَاكُ الرَّامِحُ.
The fat and goodly appearance of camels, conceived figuratively as their protective weapons.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: In the expression أَخَذَتِ الإِبِلُ سِلَاحَهَا or بِأَسْلِحَتِهَا, the camels have become fat and thereby less vulnerable to slaughter.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A man who has or carries a weapon; an armed man.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A possessive adjective describing someone equipped with weapons.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A she-camel that has voided excrement after eating herbs or leguminous plants.
A plant or herb associated with effects on camels, including increased milk, fattening, or thin excrement when eaten.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The name covers several reported botanical descriptions and is not tied to one securely identified modern species.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A frontier or fortified place of arms and observation where people watch for the enemy.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A military observation position, especially on the frontier of a hostile territory.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An armed party stationed to guard a frontier or to scout ahead of an army.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The party may explore the route, gather intelligence, prevent enemy entry, and warn of an approaching force.

cautions: The four Quranic occurrences are inflected forms of the plural أَسْلِحَةٌ; the public headword is the supported singular سِلَاحٌ.

The root contains several distinct vocalized lexical branches, including weapon, excrement, plant, and military-location usages; they should not be conflated solely because their consonantal root is the same.
